criteria.name: Introduction: mission concept and rationale - Include the following required information: • What is the spacecraft's primary mission? • Why is the mission needed? • How many spacecraft are used and why? • Who are the users (operator and customers)?
criteria.reasoning: Mission purpose (coral reef/bleaching monitoring for the GBR), rationale with statistics and citations [1]-[4], spacecraft count justified, and users/operator identified. User discussion is hedged ('likely') and citations are bare URLs rather than full references, so not top-band.

evidence.quote: The ZYZZsat however, does not require such constant coverage as the reef bleaching events occur over days and weeks. Thus, only one satellite is required.
The proposed satellite would likely be used by governmental and science agencies (e.g. CSIRO, BOM) for research and/or education.

criteria.name: Main body: mission design - Present a summary of the mission design using software and/or hand calculations as appropriate - Include relevant screenshots and software files (in the main body of the report and/or appendix) - Include the following information: • Where it will launch from, and using which launch vehicle? Why did you choose this option? • What type of orbit will you use? What are its characteristics and orbital elements? • Will you need to perform any orbital maneuvers? • Which ground control facilities will you use? • How often will your spacecraft be able to communicate with ground control? • How long will the mission last, and what are your plans for EOL?
criteria.reasoning: All major items (Kourou/Vega E, SSO elements table, access table, 5-year life, drag-sail EOL) are covered with STK evidence and an inclination-altitude calculation. However, the resolution/swath logic is inverted, no GSD/link/mass budget supports the 600 km choice, and the EOL 'no thrusters' claim contradicts the earlier statement that a manoeuvre occurs at EOL.

evidence.quote: A very high altitude would yield low resolution images which is also desirable.
An average contact duration of almost ten minutes was achieved, in addition to the already frequent amount of passes.
However, the ZYZZsat is without thrust capability and so must use a ‘passive’ strategy.

criteria.name: Conclusion
criteria.reasoning: Conclusions are tied to the design decisions (launch vehicle plus fallback, SSO illumination, Mt Pleasant station) and state the expected benefit. They remain qualitative and omit key numbers (contact statistics, element values), so low Accomplished.

evidence.quote: A specific launch vehicle – the Vega E – has been selected although it has not been built yet. Thus, launch may need to be adjusted

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Good overall structure (executive summary, TOC, headed sections, conclusion, bibliography) and readable prose. But figures are captioned without numbers, all tables are unlabelled, the EOL paragraph is truncated mid-sentence, and the bibliography is bare URLs including Wikipedia, so referencing does not meet the required standard.

evidence.quote: It acts like a regular sail, utilising a large surface area to ‘ and is suitable for low-earth orbit altitudes

technical_issues.issue: Claim that a very high altitude would give low resolution 'which is also desirable' contradicts the mission requirement; no GSD/swath calculation justifies 600 km for a 250 km-wide reef.
RAAN = 27.33 deg is said to indicate the launch facility location; RAAN is set by launch time/azimuth, not by the site.

Reasoning that Kourou's 5.05 deg latitude gives two daily launch windows at ascending/descending node is incorrect; no discussion of the performance penalty of a 97.8 deg retrograde injection from Kourou.

Access table duplicates access 14/15 and has inconsistent numbering; no explicit passes-per-day or data-volume/link budget; Mt Pleasant is a radio telescope, suitability for TT&C/downlink not demonstrated.
Earlier states the only manoeuvre is at EOL, later states the satellite has no thrust capability; EOL drag-sail sentence is truncated with no altitude/lifetime trade.
Suggests solar panels could 'lengthen' life, but power generation is a baseline requirement, not an optional lifetime extension.
No mass, power, data-rate or sensor specification; orbit selection not tied to actual instrument coverage requirement.

overall: Sound, well-structured mission concept with genuine STK usage and clear justification of a single SSO satellite for GBR monitoring. Technical depth is limited: no swath/GSD or link budget, inverted resolution reasoning, unlabelled figures/tables, bare-URL references including Wikipedia, and internal inconsistencies on manoeuvres and EOL.

feedback.summary: You have a sound, well-structured mission concept: a single SSO satellite for GBR bleaching monitoring, with genuine STK use and clear launch, orbit and ground-segment coverage. To reach the next level, add quantitative instrument and link budgets, correct the resolution and RAAN/launch-window reasoning, resolve the manoeuvre/EOL contradiction, and bring figures, tables and references to a professional standard.
next_steps: Add a GSD/swath calculation and a link/data-volume budget (with passes per day) to justify the 600 km orbit and Mt Pleasant downlink; include mass and power budgets.

Correct the technical inconsistencies: remove the 'low resolution is desirable' claim, explain that RAAN is set by launch time/azimuth not site, justify the retrograde injection penalty from Kourou, and make the manoeuvre/EOL story consistent (thrusters vs drag sail).
Professionalise presentation: number all figures, label all tables, complete the truncated EOL sentence, and replace bare URLs/Wikipedia with full references that match in-text citations.

criteria.C1: Strong introduction: you define the coral-reef bleaching mission, justify it with statistics and citations [1]–[4], explain why one spacecraft suffices, and identify operator and customers. For the top band, replace hedged wording ('would likely be used by') with a firm user/operator statement, and convert bare URLs into full, consistently formatted references.
criteria.C2: You cover every major design item—Kourou/Vega E, SSO elements, STK access, 5-year life and drag-sail EOL—with software evidence and an inclination–altitude calculation. To move from Adequate to Accomplished, add GSD/swath, mass, power and link budgets; correct the inverted resolution claim in Orbit and the RAAN/launch-window reasoning; fix the duplicated access entries; and resolve the 'manoeuvre at EOL' versus 'no thrust capability' contradiction.
criteria.C3: Your conclusion ties back to specific choices—Vega E with fallback, SSO illumination and Mt Pleasant—and states the expected benefit, which is appropriate. For the top band, make it quantitative: cite contact statistics, orbital element values and the expected coverage/benefit, rather than leaving the conclusions qualitative.
criteria.C4: The report is well structured with an executive summary, contents, headed sections and readable prose. To reach Accomplished, number figure captions and label every table, complete the truncated EOL sentence, and replace bare-URL references (including Wikipedia) with full formatted entries that match your in-text citations.
